fullPassage: Motivation is what helps us change ourselves, our situation, or our environment. All animals have motivation; it's what stimulates them to find food, a safe place to sleep, and a mate. Contrary to popular belief, motivation isn't a static thing that you either do or don't have. It comes and goes. All animals appear to be motivated to secure food, safety, and companionship, but basically no one wants these things all the time. As humans, we're motivated by far more than basic survival needs, but even still, we don't pursue social acceptance, fast cars, or fancy jewelry all the time. Motivation is in part a specific drive to do a specific action at a specific time, and it's highly influenced by what's going on right now. For example, people love eating, but when we've just loaded up at the buffet, we're less motivated to seek out food than if we haven't eaten in a while.

questions.passage: It comes and goes. All animals appear to be __________ (motivate) to secure food, safety, and companionship, but basically no one wants these things all the time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 'appear to be + 과거분사' 수동 구조로, 동물은 동기를 '부여받는' 대상이므로 motivate → motivated.
det.analysis: All animals appear to be __________ (motivate) → 「appear to be + 과거분사」 수동태, 동물이 동기부여되는 대상 → motivate를 motivated로
det.tip: appear to be + p.p.(motivated) = ~되는 것처럼 보이다

questions.passage: As humans, we're motivated by far more than basic survival needs, but even still, we don't pursue social __________ (accept), fast cars, or fancy jewelry all the time. Motivation is in part a specific drive to do a specific action at a specific time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 형용사 social의 수식을 받는 명사 자리이자 pursue의 목적어이므로, 동사 accept를 명사 acceptance로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: pursue social __________ (accept) → 'social(형용사) + 명사' & pursue(타동사)의 목적어 = 명사 자리 → accept(동사)를 acceptance(명사)로
det.tip: accept(동사) → acceptance(명사): social acceptance(사회적 인정)

questions.passage: Motivation is what helps us change ourselves, our situation, or our environment. All animals have motivation; it's what stimulates them to find food, a safe place to sleep, and a mate. Contrary to popular belief, motivation isn't a static thing that you either do or don't have. It comes and goes. All animals appear to be motivated to secure food, safety, and companionship, but basically no one wants these things all the time. As humans, we're motivated by far more than basic survival needs, but even still, we don't pursue social acceptance, fast cars, or fancy jewelry all the time. Motivation is in part a specific drive to do a specific action at a specific time, and it's highly influenced by what's going on right now. For example, people love eating, but when we've just loaded up at the buffet, we're less motivated to __________ than if we haven't eaten in a while.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 뷔페에서 막 잔뜩 먹었을 때는, 오랫동안 먹지 않았을 때보다 '음식을 찾아 나설(seek out food)' 동기가 덜하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① fall asleep quickly — 빨리 잠들다 (문맥 무관)
❌ ② exercise much harder — 더 열심히 운동하다 (문맥 무관)
❌ ③ share our meal — 식사를 나누다 (문맥 무관)
✅ ④ seek out food — 음식을 찾아 나서다 ←정답
det.tip: seek out food = 음식을 찾아 나서다 (배부르면 그 동기가 줄어듦)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: '음식을 덜 찾게 된다'는 결과와 '오랫동안 먹지 않았을 때와의 대조'로 보아, 빈칸은 '뷔페에서 잔뜩 먹었을(loaded up at the buffet)' 때이다.
det.analysis:

❌ ② started a strict diet — 엄격한 다이어트를 시작했다 (문맥 무관)
❌ ③ gone hungry for days — 며칠 굶었다 (결과와 반대)
✅ ④ loaded up at the buffet — 뷔페에서 잔뜩 먹었다 ←정답
det.tip: load up at the buffet = 뷔페에서 잔뜩 먹다 (그래서 음식 찾을 동기 감소)
